quote_text:
Are you feeling a  
bit bittersweet about that result? Yeah, I have mixed emotions about it  
because I feel the overriding feeling is  that we did enough in the second half to  
win the match. But in the first half, to be  honest, I thought St Johnstone were better.  
Their rotations were better, their possession  was better, and we struggled to cope with that.
They scored a good goal, and we went behind,  
but the character of the team showed—we got  straight back into it and got a goal back.  
That changes your halftime talk.  We made a couple of adjustments,  
obviously made a personnel change, but also made  a tactical change that really worked for us.
I thought, similarly to the Motherwell game, it  was a really strong second-half performance. I  
thought Tiffy's shot was going in, I thought Lyall  Cameron’s strike from the edge of the box was  
going in. I thought we were the ones pushing for  the winner. So, I’ve got to be happy with that.
But the biggest positive for me today is that I’ve  got my captain back. Even though they had a lot of  
possession, I thought we looked a more secure team  with the experience of Joe and Trevor being there,  
as well as Jordan McGee. That’s something  we’ve really been lacking this season.
Once the dust settles, knowing I’ve  got Joe back is a big positive. He  
was struggling—at 76 minutes, I looked  over, and he was cramping up. But the  
character he showed to get through the game,  that’s the biggest positive for me today.
How important is he going to be for the run-in  to the split and after the split as well? 
Hugely important. I think everybody can see that.
It has been a difficult season with the number of  injuries we’ve picked up to experienced players.  
I’ve had to expose a lot of young, inexperienced  players to situations they’ve never faced before.
As a staff, we can guide them as much as  possible from the side of the pitch and during  
the week in training, but on a matchday,  they need that experience on the pitch.
That was really evident today—the  number of times Joe got his head on  
things, the way he was organizing  everything, that’s what we need.  
And to answer your question, that will  absolutely serve us well going forward.
Was it just important to get a point on the  
board and stop the run of defeats? Yeah, that was the biggest objective  
today. Every game, I set my team out to win, but  today it was really important that we didn’t lose.
In the first half, as I said,  St Johnstone were better,  
but we showed character to get back into  the game. And for me, the honesty of the  
group was there—they admitted at halftime  that the first half had to be better. We  
responded in the second half, and I thought  we really showed intent to go and win it.
So, I’ve got to praise the mentality of the team,  and I agree with you—we’ve stopped the rot. It’s  
important now that we build on that. We’ve got  time before our next league game, the derby  
against Dundee United. We can regroup, get players  fit again, and hopefully get Scott Fraser back.
There is a feeling that hopefully  that bad run is behind us now.
Was Lyall Cameron’s substitution an injury issue? Yeah, he was feeling a little knock on his ankle.
But we looked at it and obviously had  to cope better with the rotations. I  
think the change we made absolutely helped  with that. I thought we retained possession  
a bit better, were more on the front  foot, and created more opportunities.
At this stage of the season, you have to look  at all your personnel, assess everyone who is  
available, and make the right decisions to turn  the game in your favor. I thought we did that  
in the second half. As I said, I thought we  looked the more likely team to go and win it.
How important is Simon Murray going  to be for the rest of the season? 
Hugely important. Simon goes on these runs—he’s  that type of striker. That’s his third goal in  
three games now, I think. He can go a few games  without scoring, but then he picks it up again.
He’s a constant threat.
One thing we targeted today was that  we had more height than St Johnstone,  
so we wanted to get things into  the box, win the first contact,  
and then get onto the second ball. We did that  on a few occasions. Earlier in the game, we  
won the first contact but didn’t get onto  the second ball. But for the goal, Simon  
showed his intelligence as a striker—his predatory  instincts—to get onto that second ball and score.
At this stage of the season, you really rely  on your experienced players. Joe coming back,  
Simon’s form, and hopefully getting Scott Fraser,  
Jordan McGee, and Trevor Carson back—they are  pivotal in the run-in for the rest of the season.
Thank you. Cheers.
title: Tony Docherty FULL Press Conference | Dundee 1-1 St Johnstone
